bullets: Game 4 of a seven-game single-deck video (window 733.9s-914.9s): the eight highest-rated cards on RoyaleAPI played as one list. Ryley's own verdict on it at t=749-760: 'this just looks like a regular very solid bridge spam deck, but it is literally the eight highest ranked cards in the game... I'm going to call this a perfect deck.'

Piloted as two-lane bridge pressure, not as a single push: Elite Barbarians at [14, 13] (clock 2:45) with Battle Ram at [2, 12] (clock 2:30), then Ebarbs at [3, 13] (1:58) and Ram at [2, 13] (1:39), then Ebarbs at [14, 13] again (1:13). The enemy left tower goes 4858 -> 2885 before clock 2:11.

The bridge timing is keyed to the opponent's elixir, not his own: 'Let's go for the Evo Ebs here at the bridge again because he did use a little bit of stuff' (t=789), 'I was thinking that he did use a lot of good cards for the Ebarbs, so just going them at the bridge could get us good value' (t=802-809).

Heal Spirit and Zap exist to keep those pushes connecting rather than to defend - the Heal Spirit behind the bridge Ebarbs at clock 1:57 produces 'a thousand damage' (t=796-798), and all three Zaps of the game are cast on the opponent's half.

Defence is a two-card package: Cannon Cart centre on his own half ([9, 10] clock 1:23, [8, 8] at 0:50 and 0:20) and Barbarian Barrel on the left ([3, 9], [3, 10], [3, 11]), with the Barrel often played as a prediction against the opponent's champion ability (t=860-863).

Mother Witch plus Goblinstein is the late-game engine: she is played defensively for the Cursed Hogs at clock 0:40 ('just to start spawning some royal hogs', t=867), then everything after that protects her - Goblinstein at the bridge at 0:11 and two Battle Rams used as Lightning blocks (t=870, t=905).

Result: a win with almost no damage taken - own towers finish 4818/4858 against an enemy left tower reading 299-214, and the opponent concedes on air ('He's calling it good game. He kind of knows it', t=902; 'that is good game. Very beautiful win', t=907).

new_deck.rationale: Two fast bridge threats (Elite Barbarians and Battle Ram) played on a full elixir bar in alternating lanes, backed by cheap spells and a single defensive troop - which is exactly how Ryley describes it on air: 'a regular very solid bridge spam deck'.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The deck attacks with a 6-elixir pair and a 4-elixir ram that both threaten immediately at the bridge, so the opponent has to answer in two lanes within seconds and can never bank elixir for their own win condition. Heal Spirit and Zap are the glue: for one and two elixir they turn an Elite Barbarians drop that would have been cleaned up into a connection, which is where the bulk of this match's tower damage came from. Defence is deliberately thin - Cannon Cart centre on his own half plus Barbarian Barrel for swarms - because the deck expects to be ahead on tower damage and only needs to survive counterattacks, not win them. The late game shifts to Mother Witch and Goblinstein: she converts the opponent's defensive swarm into Cursed Hogs while the Goblinstein Monster forces a second answer at the bridge, and Ryley protects that pair by using the Battle Ram's Barbarians as a Lightning shield rather than by holding a spell.
